name: claude-motion
description: A motion design toolkit for coding agents.
readme_summary: Claude-motion is a JavaScript toolkit that empowers coding agents to create sophisticated motion graphics and web-based simulations. It provides agents with 'taste' by teaching them motion design principles, enabling self-review of frames, and integrating a sound engine for audio generation. The toolkit also facilitates the conversion of web simulations into high-frame-rate videos.
key_features: Motion design rules and presets for agents
Self-review loop for frame analysis and correction
Integrated sound engine for audio generation (typing, clicks, whooshes, etc.)
Pipeline for rendering web simulations (HTML, three.js) into 60 fps video
Frame-exact capture using headless Chromium and ffmpeg
Works with Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, and other agent frameworks via AGENTS.md
primary_use_case: To enable AI coding agents to autonomously generate high-quality motion graphics and video content from simulations or design specifications.
cover_image_prompt: A sophisticated AI 'conductor' standing at a digital podium, orchestrating a symphony of light and motion. Swirls of code and data streams flow from the podium, transforming into vibrant, animated visual elements like abstract shapes, text animations, and dynamic transitions that fill the scene. Subtle visual cues like a timeline with beat markers and a small monitor displaying frame-by-frame analysis indicate the process. The overall mood is creative and precise, with a clean, futuristic aesthetic. The style should be a 3D isometric illustration with glowing neon accents and a dark, sophisticated background, emphasizing the transformation of raw code into polished visual art.

name: stargazer
description: Turn your GitHub stargazers into cinematic 1600x900 social cards and 60fps MP4 loops directly in your browser.
readme_summary: Stargazer is a browser-based tool that transforms GitHub stargazers and contributors into visually appealing social media cards and animated MP4 loops. It focuses on client-side processing for privacy and real-time previews, allowing users to celebrate project milestones with custom designs.
primary_use_case: Creating shareable social media assets (cards and videos) to celebrate GitHub project milestones like reaching star count goals.
cover_image_prompt: A celestial cartographer in a dimly lit observatory, using a magical astrolabe to map constellations formed by glowing GitHub stars. The astrolabe projects intricate, cinematic social cards and shimmering MP4 video loops onto a large screen, celebrating the charting of new cosmic milestones. Subtle UI elements resembling a clean, modern web interface are visible on a nearby console, displaying stargazer counts and theme options. The scene is rendered in a 3D isometric illustration style, with a focus on deep blues, purples, and glowing golden accents, conveying a sense of wonder and digital achievement.

name: Animator
readme_summary: Animator is a Python tool that automatically generates narrated, hand-drawn whiteboard explainer videos from a simple text prompt. It leverages AI to write scripts, draw scenes, record narration, and animate elements in sync with the spoken words.
key_features: Generates narrated whiteboard explainer videos from text prompts
AI-powered scriptwriting, scene drawing, and narration
Supports custom images and audio for video creation
No GPU required, runs locally on CPU
primary_use_case: Creating explainer videos automatically from text prompts for educational or informational content.
cover_image_prompt: A magical quill pen is rapidly writing a story onto a digital scroll. As each word appears, it transforms into a hand-drawn icon or simple animation on a whiteboard surface that seamlessly flows into the next scene. A disembodied voice bubble emanates from the scroll, synchronized with the drawing. Subtle code snippets and data streams flow around the scene, indicating the underlying technology. The overall mood is creative and efficient, with a clean, bright aesthetic. The style should be a 3D isometric illustration with clear, bold lines and a vibrant color palette.

name: shellfirm
description: Safety guardrails for ai coding agents and human terminal commands
readme_summary: Shellfirm acts as a safety net for terminal commands, protecting against accidental or malicious execution by both humans and AI agents. It intercepts commands, analyzes their potential risk, and can present challenges or suggest safer alternatives before execution.
key_features: Support for 8 shells (Zsh, Bash, Fish, etc.)
MCP server for AI agent integration (Claude Code, Cursor)
primary_use_case: Preventing dangerous or unintended shell command execution by humans and AI agents.
cover_image_prompt: A vigilant, stylized robot hand acting as a gatekeeper, holding up a digital shield that displays a 'STOP' sign. In front of the shield, a chaotic stream of digital code and command lines is being forcefully redirected by the shield's energy. On one side of the shield, a few 'safe' command lines are allowed to pass through, glowing with a soft green light. The background is a clean, modern terminal interface with subtle data visualizations. The overall mood is protective and reassuring, with a focus on preventing harm. The art style should be a 3D isometric illustration with a futuristic, clean aesthetic, emphasizing clarity and safety.

name: ggwave
readme_summary: ggwave is a tiny C++ library that enables data transmission through sound waves, including ultrasound. It uses a simple FSK modulation and error correction codes to ensure robust communication between air-gapped devices, supporting various platforms like Arduino and Python.
key_features: Supports RAW waveform generation and analysis
Works with any audio backend via callbacks
primary_use_case: Enabling data communication between devices using audible or ultrasonic sound waves, particularly useful for air-gapped systems or simple device pairing.
cover_image_prompt: A conceptual illustration of two stylized, air-gapped speakers facing each other across a subtle digital divide. One speaker emits a visible, colorful sound wave that transforms into a stream of binary data as it travels. The other speaker receives this data stream, which then coalesces into a small, glowing icon representing information (like a document or a key). The background is a clean, minimalist gradient, with subtle circuit board patterns faintly visible. Small, abstract UI elements with the 'ggwave' logo are subtly integrated into the speaker designs. The overall mood is one of seamless, invisible communication. Style: 3D isometric illustration with soft, glowing effects and a focus on clear visual flow.
